questions.prompt: In Strategy Based Diagnostics, what does the diagnostic trouble code actually tell you?
questions.explanation: A code sets when a test fails under set conditions. It directs testing; it does not condemn a part by itself.

options.label: A
options.body: The fault area and the conditions the module detected - it is the starting point for testing, not proof that a named part has failed

options.label: B
options.body: The exact part to replace without further testing

options.label: C
options.body: That the fault is intermittent and can be ignored

options.label: D
options.body: That the wiring has already been proven good

questions.prompt: You start work on a case covered by Onboard Diagnostics Generation One. What is the correct first step?
questions.explanation: Strategy-based work starts with verification and data. Freeze frame shows the conditions when the fault set.

options.label: A
options.body: Replace the most commonly failed part for that code

options.label: B
options.body: Clear the codes and return the vehicle

options.label: C
options.body: Disconnect the battery and wait for the relearn

options.label: D
options.body: Verify the complaint, check for DTCs and freeze-frame data, and review service information for that system

questions.prompt: When testing for Onboard Diagnostics Key Elements, which measurement approach gives a trustworthy result?
questions.explanation: Faults are condition-dependent. Testing under the set conditions and comparing to spec separates a real fault from a one-off reading.

options.label: A
options.body: Rely on the code description instead of measuring

options.label: B
options.body: Back-probe every wire until one reads battery voltage

options.label: C
options.body: Measure under the conditions that set the fault, compare to specification, and watch the live reading change as conditions change

options.label: D
options.body: Measure once, key off, on a cold engine only

questions.prompt: A confirmed fault in Onboard Diagnostics Key Elements Two most directly points to which cause?
questions.explanation: The fault description narrows the cause. Confirm it with voltage, resistance and live-data checks before replacing anything.

options.label: A
options.body: Old engine oil changing the electrical signal

options.label: B
options.body: A circuit, connection or component fault in that system, proven by measuring the circuit rather than guessing from the code alone

options.label: C
options.body: A discharged battery on every vehicle with this code

options.label: D
options.body: Low tire pressure changing the module calculation

questions.prompt: On a scan tool, what should you check first for Understanding Diagnostic Trouble Codes?
questions.explanation: Related PIDs, freeze frame and companion codes show whether the fault is in the sensor, the circuit, or a shared power/ground.

options.label: A
options.body: The related live data PID against a known-good value, plus freeze frame and any related codes set at the same time

options.label: B
options.body: Only the odometer reading

options.label: C
options.body: The radio volume PID

options.label: D
options.body: Whether the code can be cleared from the home screen

questions.prompt: Before condemning a component in Understanding Drive Cycles, which wiring check is essential?
questions.explanation: Many 'failed parts' are terminal and voltage-drop problems. A circuit that cannot carry load will make a good part read faulty.

options.label: A
options.body: Wiggle the harness once and replace the part if nothing changes

options.label: B
options.body: Check only the fuse and stop there

options.label: C
options.body: Spray every connector with water and watch for a change

options.label: D
options.body: Inspect the connector for spread, corroded or backed-out terminals, then load-test or voltage-drop the power, ground and signal circuits

questions.prompt: What component-level test best supports a diagnosis in Drive Cycles Diagnostics?
questions.explanation: A component is condemned only when its own measured output is out of specification on circuits already proven good.

options.label: A
options.body: Hit the component lightly and listen for a rattle only

options.label: B
options.body: Read the part number and order a replacement on that alone

options.label: C
options.body: Test the component against its specification - resistance, signal output or response to a commanded change - and compare it with the circuit tests already done

options.label: D
options.body: Swap in a part from another vehicle and hope the code stays away

questions.prompt: During a Control Module Power and Ground Circuit Checks case, which practice should be avoided?
questions.moduleTitle: Control Module Power and Ground Circuit Checks
questions.explanation: Untested parts swapping destroys the evidence in the original fault and makes the next diagnosis harder, not easier.

options.label: A
options.body: Road testing after a repair

options.label: B
options.body: Parts swapping without test results, because it can mask the fault, add new faults, and waste the customer's money

options.label: C
options.body: Recording measurements before clearing codes

options.label: D
options.body: Checking service information and TSBs

questions.prompt: After repairing a fault found under Strategy Based Diagnostics, how do you verify the repair?
questions.explanation: Verification means the enabling monitor actually ran. A cleared code that has not re-run its monitor is not a proven repair.

options.label: A
options.body: Clear the codes, run the drive cycle or operating conditions that enable the monitor, and confirm the monitor runs and passes with no code returning

options.label: B
options.body: Clear the codes in the bay and release the vehicle immediately

options.label: C
options.body: Drive around the block once with the scan tool disconnected

options.label: D
options.body: Turn the warning lamp bulb check off

questions.prompt: Two tests disagree during Onboard Diagnostics Generation One - the live data looks normal but the fault returns under load. What is the best next move?
questions.explanation: Intermittent and load-dependent faults show up only under their set conditions. Graphing through the event captures the dropout.

options.label: A
options.body: Replace both the sensor and the module at once

options.label: B
options.body: Tell the customer the fault is normal

options.label: C
options.body: Erase the code history so it cannot return

options.label: D
options.body: Recreate the exact freeze-frame conditions and graph or record the data through the fault, checking for dropouts and intermittent connections
